title: ohmyho.st
description: Agent-first application hosting with Postgres, files, email and domains, using GitHub or managed source through a CLI, MCP tools and a typed API.
body:
[ohmyho.st](https://ohmyho.st), also reachable through [omh.st](https://omh.st), is an application-hosting platform I am building for developers and coding agents. Hosting, Postgres, files, transactional email and domains are managed through the same CLI, MCP tools and typed API.

## From an agent conversation to a running application

An agent can inspect an existing project, save a version, build it in Dev and publish a verified version to Prod. The platform supports connected GitHub repositories and managed source, so an application can also be developed from a connected chat. Existing projects retain their source connection and environment choices as work continues.

## A portable stack for AI-built products

The hosting workflow covers supported Next.js, Astro, Vite and TanStack applications with managed services. The customer-side CLI, MCP integration, SDK and runtime packages are open source; the hosted platform is a separate service.

## Recent work

On 17 October, native Astro support shipped for both static sites and Cloudflare Workers server rendering. I migrated this journal, sebmer.com, to Astro and verified the same build through Dev and Prod. The public Astro hosting guides were refined on 18 October.

The October work added managed source and OAuth-based access for native agent conversations, then improved recovery so an interrupted operation can continue from its saved state.

On 9 October, opt-in Postgres row-level-security support gave applications another way to scope database access. The 10 October release expanded Next.js support, including Cache Components, and improved framework compatibility checks.

On 13 October, I fixed managed Postgres provisioning on Neon’s Free plan and verified database reads and writes in Dev and Prod. The 16 October client release exposed account email and organization names across the API, CLI and MCP, helping agents identify the selected account and workspace.

## Why I am building it

An agent that writes software also needs a practical way to run it and manage the services around it. This project makes those steps inspectable and repeatable, from the first application version to ongoing operations.

[Visit ohmyho.st](https://ohmyho.st) or [read the documentation](https://docs.ohmyho.st/).
